fields.description:
## Problem

`infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py` prices CloudWatch token counts
using a rate table derived daily from Cost Explorer and matched to models by
string heuristics. That layer produced four defects in the twelve days after
deployment (2026-09-12), all one class — matching model identifiers against
billing labels by substring and suffix. The instances were a direction-suffix
collision in `_rate_for`/`_match` resolving input to cache-write for
version-suffix-free ModelIds; a `_normalise` label/id mismatch
(`Nova2.0Lite` vs `us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0`) dropping a model to
`UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K`; the `BEDROCK_SERVICE_VALUES` allowlist
(3083-ada3-3a0f-4051) omitting five live services, leaving the CE signal at about
a third of real spend; and `MARKETPLACE_TOKEN_SUFFIXES` handling only CamelCase
while AWS also bills snake_case and `_Global`. Two reached production unalarmed,
one for seven days.

## Approach

Price every token at a ceiling rate for its direction, set above the highest
per-direction rate observed on this account, so the estimate is an upper bound and
the cap cannot fire late. Per UTC day:

    spend = max( sum over regions and the four token metrics of
                   undimensioned CloudWatch Sum * CEILING[metric],
                 ce_spend )

`AWS/Bedrock` publishes a zero-dimension series per token metric, requested by
sending `Dimensions: []` (omitting the key is not equivalent). Over 2026-09-14 to
09-24 it equalled the per-ModelId sum exactly, 930,831,660 tokens both ways. That
equivalence is an external-system assumption the criteria below require
re-verifying before the undimensioned read ships. The estimate reads exactly those
four aggregates per region and never adds per-ModelId series — today's handler
reads only per-ModelId series because mixing the two double-counts.

Cost Explorer stays in enforcement: it is the only signal covering Bedrock spend
publishing no token metric (Cohere Rerank is live; provisioned throughput and
batch are structural), and it is orthogonal to all four defects.

**Release discriminator.** An all-empty CloudWatch read is ambiguous: it is both a
metrics gap and the normal idle/new-UTC-day state the automatic release depends
on. CE cannot disambiguate it, since CE lags 8-24h and reads zero for hours into a
busy day. Instead the handler persists the day's highest observed token total,
keyed by UTC date so a new day starts absent. An empty read may release only when
today's key is present and zero-valued; an absent key with a deny attached holds
the deny, which also covers a mid-day deploy over old state. A partial-region
failure holds the deny, since the surviving region is a floor. The mark governs
release only: on the trip side an empty read yields a zero estimate and CE remains
the other arm of the max(), so a gap cannot manufacture a trip.

**Accepted limitation.** Ceiling pricing over-estimates cheaper models; the
cheapest here are two orders of magnitude below and two bill nothing for
cache-write, so the factor is unbounded and a large embedding job can trip the cap
at a fraction of intended spend. Accepted for simplicity; the remedy is an
exact-match `{ModelId: rate}` override defaulting to the ceiling, equality only.
Documenting this, the recorded fixtures and the drift guard are the dependent story
be3d-712b-c1ac-442b, which also re-adds the `cloudwatch:ListMetrics` grant dropped
here, since its attribution needs it.

## Figures

Machine-local policy bars spend totals and bill figures from the tracker, because
the tickets branch auto-pushes to the public GitHub mirror. Every input is
derivable, so no executor depends on a private note:

- intended daily cap: the value already configured as `var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd`,
  unchanged here.
- `CEILING[d]`: 1.25x the highest per-token rate for direction `d` across all
  Bedrock services in the trailing 60 days of Cost Explorer.
- threshold: the intended daily cap scaled by the median of
  (undimensioned tokens x CEILING) / (CE Bedrock total) over those UTC days in the
  same window whose CE Bedrock total exceeds one twentieth of the intended daily
  cap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The undimensioned-versus-per-ModelId token equivalence is re-run over a fresh
  ten-day window and is exactly equal per region and per metric. If it diverges,
  the work halts and escalates rather than shipping the undimensioned read.
  Checked: the comparison output recorded as a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] The seven pricing functions (`_refresh_rates`, `_rate_for`, `_seed_for`,
  `_normalise`, `_strip_billing_region`, `_marketplace_rate_key`,
  `_rate_key_for_ce_group`) and six constants (`SEED_RATES`, `RATE_OVERRIDES`,
  `BEDROCK_SERVICE_VALUES`, `MARKETPLACE_TOKEN_SUFFIXES`, `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K`,
  `MARKETPLACE_TOKENS_PER_RATE_UNIT`) are absent from the module.
- [ ] The `TOKEN_METRICS` direction multipliers are removed.
- [ ] The imports left unreferenced by those removals — `re` and `typing.Literal`
  — are removed. Checked: `make lint` flags an unused import.
- [ ] The module docstring no longer describes a derived rate table, seed rates,
  `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K` or a daily rate refresh.
- [ ] `_metered_spend` issues exactly four undimensioned `GetMetricData` queries
  per region, each sending `Dimensions: []`.
- [ ] `_metered_spend` calls no `list_metrics`.
- [ ] The `cloudwatch:ListMetrics` action is removed from the execution role's
  `ReadSpendSignals` statement, leaving `ce:GetCostAndUsage` and
  `cloudwatch:GetMetricData`.
- [ ] A `CEILING` mapping gives one rate per token metric, each at least the
  highest rate for that direction over the trailing 60 days of Cost Explorer, with
  the derivation recorded as a comment beside it.
- [ ] Enforcement compares `max(ceiling_estimate, ce_spend)`. Checked: a test
  driving each arm larger in turn.
- [ ] `_ce_spend_today` classifies Bedrock spend by predicate (service equals
  `Amazon Bedrock` or ends with the Bedrock Edition suffix), not an allowlist.
  Checked: a test over a stub carrying all ten live services, including the five
  the allowlist omitted.
- [ ] The day's high-water token total is persisted keyed by UTC date.
- [ ] An empty read with today's key present and zero-valued may release. Checked:
  a test on a fresh day.
- [ ] An empty read after a nonzero reading that day holds the deny. Checked: a
  test seeding the mark.
- [ ] An empty read with today's key absent and a deny attached holds the deny.
  Checked: a test loading pre-change state mid-day.
- [ ] A partial-region failure holds the deny. Checked: a test raising in one
  region while the other returns data below threshold.
- [ ] Any exception from a metered or CE read fails closed. Checked: a test
  raising from each client in turn.
- [ ] `infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf` carries the threshold and warning
  values derived above.
- [ ] The `SEED_RATES`, `RATE_OVERRIDES`, `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K` and
  `RATE_WINDOW_DAYS` environment entries are deleted, along with whichever
  `variable` or `locals` blocks are left unreferenced. Checked: `terraform plan`
  shows exactly those deletions, the IAM action removal, and the threshold and
  warning changes.
- [ ] No unused Terraform declarations remain. Checked: `terraform validate`.
- [ ] `state["rates"]`, `state["rates_day"]`, `metered_estimated`, `MeteredRate`
  and its `RateSource` alias, and the `" (estimated)"` rendering are removed.

## Testing

Every criterion is proved by
`env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -q`,
except the Terraform ones, proved via
`python3 scripts/terraform_prod.py plan --out <scratch>/plan.tfplan` and
`terraform validate`, the unused-import one, proved by `make lint`, and the
equivalence re-run, proved by its recorded output.
`make lint`/`make typecheck` gate commits; `make verify` runs before push.

## Rollback

Set `DRY_RUN=true` to halt attach and detach while keeping the function
observable. Full back-out: revert the Gerrit change and re-run the mediated plan
and apply, restoring prior code, env and IAM exactly.
